question.problem:
A function $f(x)$ has values according to the table below:

| $x$ | $-3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.9$ | $0.4$ | $0.1$ | $0$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ | $0.9$ |

Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=-1$ using a backward difference approximation.
question.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x)-f(x-h)}{h}
$$

 

at the point $x=-1.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case, $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(-1) & ≈\frac{f(-1)-f(-1-1)}{1} \\  & =\frac{f(-1)-f(-2)}{1} \\  & =\frac{0.1-0.4}{1} \\  & =-0.3.\end{aligned}
$$
